title: Keep directions apart from the words
statement: Keep directions on how to read apart from the words to be read, and let them set only the tone: one voice model read its own instructions aloud.
detail:
One voice model read its own style instructions aloud at the start of all four of its takes (finding 6,
`othello-unit-video/research/FINDINGS.md`). The research record cites the model's documentation as treating the text
field strictly as a verbatim transcript, with sustained style in a separate field
(https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/speech-generation). The kit's rule is
that the direction sets the register only and ends by saying that no words may be added or changed
(`othello-unit-video/.claude/skills/uvk-narration-make/SKILL.md`), and the lesson engine's narrator sends no direction
at all (`g9/transformer/src/providers.js`).
against:
the kit's own narration tool still sends the direction and the
script as one string (`unit-video-kit/tools/narration/generate_takes.py`), and no peer-reviewed study of this was found.

evidence.quote: - The shipped DBQ source packs included self-advocacy/meta text in document content:
- Local IB treated that as evaluation-gaming and zeroed DBQ.
- Important negative lesson: adding modern summaries inside DBQ `content` made relevance better but failed factual/stimulus quality because IB treats that as fabricated primary-source text.
- Spoken lines never open with "Name:" — the TTS drops the label silently (speaker-label trap,
"remove Scout's interjections at the top of each page. They take away from the reading flow."
Context belongs in source labels/rubrics, not document content.
The text goes alone, with no style instruction (a 3.8 voice read its instruction aloud, 6 Oct).
